description: A Chief Patent Counsel must approve a resolution package for an employee's inventorship dispute before the company's patent application is filed, including the payment, inventorship record, assignment, confidentiality terms, and counsel review process, with input from employment, patent, HR, and conflicts counsel.

shared_context.S1: A former engineer claims that she contributed to the conception of a machine-learning hardware invention for which the company plans to file a patent application in three weeks.
shared_context.S2: The current draft resolution would pay the engineer $50,000, identify the company employee currently listed in the draft as the sole inventor, and use broad mutual confidentiality language.
shared_context.S3: Maya Chen has final authority to approve the resolution and the related patent-filing instructions.
shared_context.S4: The firm's routine pre-approval process requires patent, employment, HR, and conflicts counsel to report relevant case-file and business information before Maya makes the final call.

PF1.text: While reviewing the inventor's lab notebook and source-control records, Elias confirmed that the engineer contributed to conception of the claimed improvement. She must be listed as a co-inventor, and her assignment must be recorded before the application is filed; Elias has not yet amended the inventorship checklist.

PF2.text: Nina's compensation review of comparable invention disputes supports exactly $72,000 for this resolution, payable through payroll as wages rather than as an independent-contractor fee; she completed the review yesterday but has not circulated the memorandum.

PF3.text: In a meeting this week, the engineer told Samir that public recognition as a named inventor is her primary concern, and she will accept only a mutual non-disparagement clause rather than broad confidentiality restrictions; Samir recorded this in his HR notes but has not added it to the draft.

PF4.text: Laura's conflicts review found that the firm previously represented the engineer's startup on a related patent matter. Because that conflict cannot be waived for this resolution, independent employment counsel must review the final agreement before execution; Laura has not yet placed the conflict memorandum in the deal folder.

acceptance_conditions: The payment must be processed through payroll as wages.
The engineer must be listed as a co-inventor.
The engineer's assignment must be recorded before the patent application is filed.
The agreement must include public recognition of the engineer as a named inventor.
The agreement must use mutual non-disparagement only rather than broad confidentiality restrictions.
Independent employment counsel must review the final agreement before execution.
The payment, inventorship, assignment, recognition, and independent-review obligations must be recorded as commitments.

decisive_facts.why: The notebook and source-control review changes the filing from sole inventorship without a pre-filing assignment to naming the engineer as co-inventor and recording her assignment before filing.
The compensation review changes the draft payment from $50,000 to exactly $72,000 and changes its treatment from an unspecified settlement payment to payroll wages.
The engineer's stated priority changes the agreement from broad confidentiality to mutual non-disparagement only and adds a commitment to publicly recognize her as a named inventor.
The related prior representation changes the approval process from ordinary internal review to mandatory independent employment-counsel review before execution.
